To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
within-person variability in personality states is large and systematic, and is systematically associated with the short-term pursuit and attainment of approach and avoidance goals.

(1) the within-individual variability of Big-5 states is substantial; (2) the magnitude of within-individual Big-5 state variability is equal or larger than between-individual differences; (3) within-individual variability is larger or similar to the magnitude of other constructs assessed with the state approach; and (4) the magnitude of Big-5 state variation is not random, but is systematic and predictable.

(a) there is considerable within-individual variability over time in Big-5 personality traits; (b) this variability is larger than between-individual differences; (c) this variability is systematically associated with short-term goals; (d) this variability mediates the association between goals (e.g., approach-avoidance) and subjective well-being; and (e) this variability is associated with subjective well-being.
In summary, our research is concerned with
within-individual variability of Big-5 traits, and its implications for understanding short-term goal pursuit and subjective well-being in daily life.
the within-individual variability of Big-5 traits, and its relation to short-term goals and subjective well- being.
the within-individual variability of personality states and their relation to well-being.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study shows that the Big Five personality states are important in the daily lives of individuals.
the within-person variability in neuroticism and extroversion is as large as the between-person differences and is related to short-term goal setting and subjective well-being.
personality states are important, and that their study should be an integral part of personality research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
within-person variability is an important aspect of personality and that it is important to take it into account when studying personality and its relation to other variables.
personality traits, goals, and well-being are not static, fixed characteristics of individuals.
personality states are a powerful and useful concept for personality psychology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

personality states are a useful construct to study in their own right, as well as to understand the within-person dynamics of other important psychological constructs such as short-term goals and subjective well being.
personality states matter, and they matter a lot.
the study of personality dynamics is not a luxury.
